title: Finite type algebras preserve Noetherian spectra
statement: Let $R$ and $B$ be commutative rings with identity and let $R\to B$ be a unital homomorphism. Suppose that $B$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by finitely many elements, equivalently there is a surjective $R$-algebra map $R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to B$ for some integer $d\geq0$. If the Zariski topological space underlying $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is Noetherian, then the Zariski topological space underlying $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is Noetherian. Here a topological space is Noetherian if every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes; no ascending-chain condition on all ideals of $R$ is assumed. Zero rings are permitted.

source.place: J. Ohm and R. L. Pendleton, Rings with Noetherian spectrum, Duke Math. J. 35 (1968), pp. 631–639, Theorem 2.5 (polynomial extension) and Corollary 2.6 (finite type algebras). WANTED: not present in the local literature collection.

proof.text: Use the equivalent criterion that every open subset is compact. Every subset of a Noetherian space is compact, so every subspace is Noetherian; the union of two Noetherian subspaces is Noetherian by intersecting an arbitrary subset with both pieces and taking the union of the two compact intersections. Set pi:Spec R[T] to Spec R to be contraction along constants. Induct on closed subsets Z of Spec R, with claim that pi inverse image of Z is Noetherian. The empty case is immediate. If Z is reducible, cover it by two proper closed intersections and use induction and the union argument.

source.place: Paragraph (2), affine-chart Noetherianity input; independent agent proof formalized by H1.

proof.text: For nonempty irreducible closed Z, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] gives Z=V(p) with p prime; concretely take the vanishing ideal of Z. The quotient C=R/p is a domain. The coefficientwise quotient R[T] to C[T] is surjective, with kernel p.map C because its coefficients vanish precisely when they lie in p. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], its spectrum is a closed embedding with range pi inverse image of Z. Contraction along the quotient commutes with contraction to constant polynomials, as checked on each constant.

source.place: Paragraph (2), affine-chart Noetherianity input; independent agent proof formalized by H1.

proof.text: For any nonzero ideal I of A[T], choose a nonzero f in I of least natural degree and put a=leadingCoeff(f), which is nonzero. For a prime q avoiding C(a), show f in q implies I contained in q by strong induction on the natural degree of g in I. The case g=0 is immediate. Otherwise minimality gives deg f <= deg g. If deg g=0 then f=C(a), contradicting f in q. In positive degree cancel the leading terms: r=C(a)g-C(leadingCoeff(g))T^(deg g-deg f)f lies in I and has smaller natural degree than g. Induction gives r in q, so C(a)g in q and primality gives g in q. Now for an open U of Spec A[T], let I be the vanishing ideal of its closed complement. Its zero locus is that complement. If I=0 then U is empty. Otherwise the preceding equivalence gives U intersect D(C(a)) = D(C(a)f). This intersection is compact: [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] identifies a basic open with a localization spectrum, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] makes that spectrum compact (Mathlib packages this as PrimeSpectrum.isCompact_basicOpen).

source.place: Paragraph (2), affine-chart Noetherianity input; independent agent proof formalized by H1.

proof.text: Apply the preceding open-subset argument to A=C=R/p. For every nonzero a in C the image W of V(a) in Spec R is closed and contained properly in Z: the zero prime of the domain C lies outside V(a), and the quotient spectrum embedding is injective. Induction makes pi inverse image of W Noetherian. Restricting the coefficientwise quotient embedding to V(C(a)) in Spec C[T] gives an inducing map into pi inverse image of W, since the contractions agree on constants. Hence V(C(a)) is Noetherian. For each open U, its intersection with V(C(a)) is compact; its intersection with D(C(a)) is compact by the preceding step, so U is compact. Thus Spec C[T], and its image pi inverse image of Z, are Noetherian. This completes the closed-set induction and proves the one-variable assertion.

source.place: Paragraph (2), affine-chart Noetherianity input; independent agent proof formalized by H1.

proof.text: Induct on n using the ring equivalences R[Fin 0]=R and R[Fin(n+1)]=(R[Fin n])[T], transporting Noetherianity along their spectrum homeomorphisms. For a finite type homomorphism f:R to B use its algebra structure and the finite-type presentation theorem to obtain a surjection R[Fin n] to B. The induced closed embedding of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] transfers Noetherianity to Spec B. No nontriviality assumption was introduced: empty spectra, zero rings, and zero variables are covered.

A regex search over every statement in dag/nodes found no duplicate. Step 1: the Noetherian-space facts are elementary and correct (Stacks 0052, topology.tex:1253). Step 2: the Noetherian induction claim P(Z) on closed subsets of the base is stated explicitly, so D4 is met. Step 3: it uses only the statements of the quotient-spectrum and minimal-prime-component Mathlib leaves to get Z=V(p) and pi^{-1}(Z)≅Spec C[T], where ker(R[T]→(R/p)[T])=pR[T]. Step 4: I checked the least-degree argument. a^N r = a^N g − (a^{N−1}q)f lies in I, so r=0 by minimality and because the domain has no zero divisors. Hence I·C_a[T]=(h), with division taken from the power basis of the monic quotient; n=0 is covered. Step 5: the increasing ideals I_i are radicals with V(I_i)=F_i, and the chain stabilizes on D(a) through clause (ii) of the basic-open leaf. Step 6: V(a) is a proper closed set, P(Z') covers it, and D(a)∪V(a) covers the space. That a depends on the chain is harmless. Step 7: induction on the number of variables plus a closed subspace finishes. Small cases tested: a non-discrete rank-one valuation ring, a field, an infinite square-zero thickening, ideals with infinitely many generators, R=0, B=0, d=0.
